findings.title: executeSink is the only data endpoint that skips runtime response validation, casting the raw wire body to SinkResponse
findings.description: Every other endpoint in this file pipes the parsed JSON through a runtime guard before returning (loadPipeline -> parsePipelineResponse, previewNode -> parsePreviewNodeResponse, savePipeline -> parseSavePipelineResponse, traceCell -> parseTraceResponse, createSubmodel -> parseSubmodelCreateResponse). executeSink instead does `return post(...)` with no `.then(parseSinkResponse)` and the function signature `Promise<SinkResponse>` forces an unchecked structural cast of whatever `res.json()` returned. There is no parseSinkResponse guard anywhere in src/types/guards.ts, and executeSink is the single data-returning endpoint absent from both client.contract.test.ts (which exercises malformed-200 rejection for the others) and from any response-shape assertion in client.test.ts (its three tests only assert the outgoing request body). This breaks the file's own invariant that backend responses fail loudly at the boundary (per CLAUDE.md: 'code should be allowed to fail loudly... far superior to a fallback which is incorrect and hard to notice'). The downstream consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-48 reads `data.status || 'ok'` and `data.message || 'Written successfully'`, so a malformed/garbage payload is silently masked by `||` fallbacks rather than surfaced — the exact 'incorrect and hard to notice' situation the codebase guards against. Practical blast radius is limited because the consumer only touches two optional string fields with fallbacks, hence not a crash, but row_count/path/format are never validated and any future consumer would trust an unverified shape.
findings.evidence: client.ts:571-580 `return post("/api/pipeline/sink", {...}, { signal, timeout })` with no parse step, vs client.ts:550 `post<unknown>("/api/pipeline/trace", body, ...).then(parseTraceResponse)`. SinkResponse defined types.ts:202-208 (status/message/row_count/path/format). No `parseSinkResponse` symbol exists (grep across frontend). Consumer SinkEditor.tsx:47-49 masks with `data.status || 'ok'` / `data.message || 'Written successfully'`.
findings.behavior_preservation: For well-formed backend responses, adding a parseSinkResponse guard returns the same object and is fully behavior-preserving; it only changes behavior for malformed payloads (which currently slip through with silent `||` fallbacks) by making them fail loudly, matching the rest of the client.

coverage.notes: Retry/backoff/abort/timeout state machine (attemptFetch + request), equal-jitter backoff math, external-signal listener cleanup (added once with {once:true}, removed in finally + on sleep resolve), 403 session-expired detection, and error-body extraction (body.detail ?? body with safe catch fallback to statusText, safe even when body is null/scalar) all reviewed and found correct. Redundant `as PreviewNodeResponse` cast at line 514 and the documented-unreachable trailing `throw lastError` at line 442 noted but judged style/no-op, not reported. checkHauteSession also lacks a guard but returns a trivial {ok:boolean} liveness shape (acceptable); executeSink is the substantive deviation. import.meta.env typing provided by vite/client per tsconfig.app.json types array.

findings.title: Chart tab silently coerces/drops non-finite series values while Statistics tab throws into the ErrorBoundary
findings.description: toQuoteRow reads each series value with Number(row[col] ?? 0). The ?? only catches null/undefined, so a genuinely-null cell becomes a fabricated 0 plotted on the chart, and a non-numeric value (e.g. the string 'n/a') becomes NaN. The Chart render path then propagates NaN into SVG geometry with no user-facing signal, whereas the Statistics tab feeds the exact same rows to computeScenarioStatsBySeries, whose readFiniteNumber THROWS on null/empty/non-finite. The result: identical preview data renders a silently-wrong/broken chart in the Chart tab but trips the panel's ErrorBoundary (App.tsx:647, replacing the whole preview with the error fallback) the instant the user switches to the Statistics tab. This is an inconsistent, silent-wrongness path that contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks' guidance.
findings.evidence: Line 50: vals[col] = Number(row[col] ?? 0)  // null -> 0 (silent fake value); 'abc' -> NaN. buildSeriesScale line 94: const v = r.values[column] ?? 0 (NaN ?? 0 === NaN, not caught) -> NaN never updates vMin/vMax. SeriesLine line 265: `...${yScale(r.values[column] ?? 0).toFixed(1)}` and lines 274-277 cx/cy=yScale(NaN) -> 'NaN' path segment + circle at NaN (invisible/broken) with no warning. Contrast optimiserScenarioStats.ts readFiniteNumber (line 31-38) which throws Error('Expected finite numeric value...') for the same null/'abc' cell; computeScenarioStatsBySeries is called from line 528-536 inside a useMemo, so the throw during render hits ErrorBoundary name="NodePreview" at App.tsx:647. Same data -> silent broken chart vs hard error fallback depending only on which tab is active.

findings.title: Duplicated quote-ID truncation with inconsistent threshold and ellipsis glyph
findings.description: The same 'truncate the current quote id for display' behaviour is hand-rolled twice with different limits and different ellipsis characters: the nav header truncates at length > 12 to slice(0,10) + ASCII '...', while the sidebar truncates at length > 14 to slice(0,12) + Unicode '…'. A single shared helper (e.g. truncateMiddle/truncateEnd(id, n)) would remove the duplication and the visual inconsistency where the two displays of one id can disagree on whether/how it is shortened.
findings.evidence: Line 599: {currentQuoteId.length > 12 ? currentQuoteId.slice(0, 10) + "..." : currentQuoteId}. Lines 716-718: {currentQuoteId.length > 14 ? currentQuoteId.slice(0, 12) + "…" : currentQuoteId}. Different cutoff (12 vs 14), different prefix length (10 vs 12), different ellipsis ('...' vs '…').
findings.behavior_preservation: Behaviour-preserving only if both call sites are unified to one rule; choosing one threshold/glyph is a deliberate, tiny visual normalisation.

findings.title: allSeriesKey = JSON.stringify(allSeries) recomputed every render despite single effect-only use
findings.description: allSeriesKey is computed unconditionally on every render via JSON.stringify, but its sole consumer is the dependency array of the checked-series sync effect (lines 454-457, with exhaustive-deps disabled). Since allSeries is already a memoized stable reference (lines 424-431), the effect could simply depend on allSeries directly (set membership re-syncs only when the memo identity changes), removing both the per-render stringify and the eslint-disable. If a value-based key is genuinely desired it should be wrapped in useMemo keyed on allSeries.
findings.evidence: Line 434: const allSeriesKey = JSON.stringify(allSeries) — runs on every render. Lines 454-457: useEffect(() => { setCheckedSeries(new Set(allSeries)) /* eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps */ }, [allSeriesKey]). allSeries memoized at 424-431 on [objectiveCol, constraintCols], so its reference already changes iff the series list changes.
findings.est_reduction: 1 line + 1 eslint-disable removed, plus a per-render JSON.stringify
findings.behavior_preservation: Depending on allSeries identity instead of its JSON string preserves behaviour because allSeries is memoized and only re-created when the series list changes; the resulting Set re-sync timing is identical.
